purpose: Luliconazole is a cream used to treat fungal skin infections like athlete's foot, jock itch, and ringworm. It helps clear up the rash, itching, and skin changes caused by these infections. Your doctor or pharmacist will tell you exactly which type of infection it is being used for.
how_it_works: Luliconazole works by attacking the fungus that is causing your skin infection. It blocks the fungus from making an important part of its outer wall, which it needs to survive and grow. Without that protective wall, the fungus dies off and your skin can heal.
common_side_effects: Most people tolerate this cream very well. The most common side effects are mild skin reactions right where you apply it, such as redness, itching, or a burning or stinging feeling. These are usually minor and go away on their own.
warnings: This cream is for use on the skin only — do not get it in your eyes, mouth, or vagina. If your skin reaction gets worse or you develop a rash that spreads, contact your doctor. Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding before using this medication. Keep using the cream for the full number of days your doctor recommended, even if your skin looks better, to make sure the infection is completely gone.
typical_dosing: Luliconazole cream is usually applied once a day to the affected skin area and a small border of skin around it. For athlete's foot between the toes, you typically use it for 2 weeks. For athlete's foot on the bottom or sides of the foot, jock itch, or ringworm, it is usually used for 1 week. Always follow your doctor's or pharmacist's specific instructions.
